staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged assimp checkout, and the line map below is grounded in that exact vulnerable worktree.

classification.classification_note: UBSan reports an index-out-of-bounds on `const unsigned char [256]`, and the underlying memory-safety defect is the corresponding out-of-bounds table read in `isNumeric()` caused by sign-extending a high-bit `char` before the lookup-table index.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42498653 (assimp): Index-out-of-bounds found by fuzz target assimp_fuzzer [ubsan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42498653
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / arvo_workspace/vulnerable_run.log / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The staged 5914-byte witness is passed to `Importer::ReadFileFromMemory()` with no file hint, so assimp falls back to signature-based detection; the first 200 bytes contain lowercase `indexarray`, and Stage 01's saved run log confirms that assimp selects the Open Game Engine Exchange importer. `OpenGEXImporter::InternReadFile()` reads the full blob with `TextFileToBuffer()`, which appends a trailing NUL, and then copies the resulting 5915-byte buffer into `OpenDDLParser::m_buffer`. During recursive `parseStructureBody()` descent over that malformed OpenDDL/OpenGEX text, one body step advances to a nested-header start byte whose signed `char` value is `-77` (raw byte `0xb3`); `parsePrimitiveDataType()` does not recognize a primitive token there, so the `ddl_none` branch recurses into `parseNextNode()` and `parseIdentifier()` immediately calls `isNumeric(*in)` to reject number-starting identifiers. Vulnerable `isNumeric()` indexes `chartype_table[256]` as `chartype_table[static_cast<size_t>(in)]`. On the witnessed call, the signed `char` `-77` is converted to `size_t` as `18446744073709551539`, so the table lookup goes past the 256-entry array and Stage 01 reproduces `runtime error: index 18446744073709551539 out of bounds for type 'const unsigned char [256]'` at `OpenDDLParserUtils.h:321`. The staged patch fixes this exact obligation by computing `size_t idx = static_cast<size_t>(in);` and checking `idx < sizeof(chartype_table)` before reading the table.

source.description: First OpenGEX-side materialization of the attacker-controlled in-memory file into the importer buffer later copied into `OpenDDLParser`.
source.value_from: Stage 01's run log shows assimp selected the Open Game Engine Exchange importer. At this call, `TextFileToBuffer()` reads the exact 5914-byte staged `poc` into `buffer` and appends one trailing `0` byte in `code/Common/BaseImporter.cpp:454-465`, so the later parser copy sees 5915 bytes including the terminator.
source.note: This is the first project-code read on the crashing parser path after signature-based importer selection.

sink.description: UBSan crash site. The 256-entry character-class table is read with an out-of-range index derived from a signed high-bit `char`.
sink.note: Stage 01 reproduced `runtime error: index 18446744073709551539 out of bounds for type 'const unsigned char [256]'` at this exact expression.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `isNumeric()` widens a possibly signed `char` directly to `size_t` before indexing the 256-byte lookup table, with no cast to `unsigned char` or explicit bounds check.
root_cause.note: The saved UBSan index corresponds to a signed input value of `-77` (raw byte `0xb3`). The staged patch adds an `idx < sizeof(chartype_table)` check before the lookup.

parser_admitted.description: With no file-extension hint, assimp falls back to signature-based detection. `SearchFileHeaderForToken()` lowercases the first 200 bytes and finds `indexarray` in the staged witness, and the saved run log confirms the matching importer is Open Game Engine Exchange.

tainted_value_origin.description: This parser step positions `in` on the exact nested-header start byte later passed into `parseIdentifier()` and then `isNumeric()`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: On the crashing recursive descent, the byte that survives this step and later reaches `isNumeric()` has signed value `-77`, which the saved UBSan report identifies as raw byte `0xb3` because `size_t(-77) == 18446744073709551539`. `lookForNextToken()` does not skip that byte because it is neither space, newline, nor comma.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, so Stage 02 did not add instrumentation; the chain is closed from staged source, patch, PoC bytes, the saved run log, sanitizer trace, and reproduction report only.

The saved UBSan stack is dominated by recursive parser frames and does not preserve the lower importer/harness tail. Importer selection is therefore grounded by `arvo_workspace/vulnerable_run.log` plus `ReadFileFromMemory()`/`CanRead()` source rather than by the crash stack tail itself.

The 5914-byte witness contains many repeated `indexarray ... f3 a0 81 b3 ...` clusters, and Stage 01 artifacts do not identify a unique absolute file offset for the final crashing `0xb3`. This GT records the proved source-level parser state (`in` carrying signed value `-77` at nested-header start) rather than guessing one repeated cluster.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness passes the staged 5914-byte witness into `Importer::ReadFileFromMemory()` with no hint; assimp falls back to signature-based detection, and the saved run log shows the Open Game Engine Exchange importer is selected after header scanning finds `indexarray`.
`TextFileToBuffer()` reads the full witness into `buffer`, appends a trailing NUL, and `OpenDDLParser::setBuffer()` copies that 5915-byte byte sequence into parser-owned `m_buffer`.

Recursive structure parsing eventually advances to a nested-header start byte with signed value `-77` / raw `0xb3`; no primitive token matches there, so the parser treats the same byte as the first character of another nested header and forwards it to `parseIdentifier()`.

`parseIdentifier()` asks whether that high-bit first byte starts with a digit, and vulnerable `isNumeric()` converts the signed `char` directly to `size_t` before indexing `chartype_table[256]`, producing the saved UBSan index-out-of-bounds.

fine_trace.note: Source. After signature-based importer selection, this call reads the exact 5914-byte witness into `buffer`; `TextFileToBuffer()` appends one trailing `0`, so the later parser copy sees 5915 bytes including the terminator.

`myParser.setBuffer(&buffer[0], buffer.size())` copies the importer buffer from step 1, including the appended terminator, into parser-owned `m_buffer`. All later `in` pointers and the crashing byte come from this copied buffer.

On the crashing recursive descent, this body-normalization step advances once from the current non-alphanumeric structural byte and leaves `in` on the next attacker byte that will be interpreted as a nested header start. The later UBSan index proves that byte's signed value is `-77` (raw byte `0xb3`), and `lookForNextToken()` does not skip it because it is not space, newline, or comma.

No primitive data token matches at the high-bit byte from step 3, so `type` remains `ddl_none` and the parser takes the complex-data branch. That recursive call reuses the same `in` value as the first character of another nested node header; there is no intervening check that nested headers begin with ASCII letters.

`parseNextNode()` enters `parseHeader()`, and `parseHeader()` immediately calls `parseIdentifier()` on the same byte from step 4. Before any other validation, `parseIdentifier()` asks whether the first identifier byte is numeric, so the attacker-controlled `0xb3` is passed as a signed `char` argument into `isNumeric()`.

Root cause and sink. On the witnessed call from step 5, `in` has signed value `-77` (raw byte `0xb3`). `static_cast<size_t>(in)` therefore becomes `18446744073709551539`, and the lookup indexes one of 256 `chartype_table` entries with that huge value. UBSan reports `runtime error: index 18446744073709551539 out of bounds for type 'const unsigned char [256]'` at this exact statement. The staged patch fixes the same path by checking `idx < sizeof(chartype_table)` before the table read.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: Yes. The staged `patch.diff` changes `isNumeric()` from an unchecked `chartype_table[static_cast<size_t>(in)]` lookup to `size_t idx = static_cast<size_t>(in); return idx < sizeof(chartype_table) && (chartype_table[idx] == 1);`, which constrains the table index on the witnessed signed-char path.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `docker exec gt-arvo_42498653-workspace /bin/bash -lc '/bin/arvo run'` and reproduced `runtime error: index 18446744073709551539 out of bounds for type 'const unsigned char [256]'` in `ODDLParser::isNumeric<char const>` with stack `parseIdentifier -> parseHeader`.

format.name: OpenGEX / OpenDDL-like text
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact 5914-byte witness staged in `poc`. Assimp receives it through `ReadFileFromMemory()` with no hint, signature detection lowercases the first 200 bytes and finds `indexarray`, and the selected OpenGEX importer passes the full blob into `OpenDDLParser`. During recursive structure parsing, one nested-header start byte reaching `parseIdentifier()` has raw value `0xb3` (signed `char` value `-77`), so `isNumeric()` indexes `chartype_table[256]` with `size_t(-77)` and leaves the table. This contract is limited to that witnessed parser state and does not generalize to neighboring bytes or other malformed OpenDDL layouts.
